The answer is C. In Al-Adsani v. United Kingdom (2001), the Grand Chamber held 9–8 that granting Kuwait state immunity did not violate Article 6. It found immunity to be a legitimate and proportionate limit on access to a court, so it was not in conflict with the right to a fair trial. The team note that immunity overrides any competing Convention guarantee goes further than the Court's reasoning, which was a proportionality finding, so I'm not adopting it.

CONFIDENCE: 72
